transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Alex (Solace Sec), Priya (CTO), Tom (Infra)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick run through security needs and hosting options, curious to hear top concerns from your side
[00:18] Alex (Solace Sec): yeah thanks Maya, main thing is attestations, we need SOC2 type II and ideally ISO 27001. also key control, like who holds the keys — we have a strict BYOK policy for some workloads
[00:34] Priya (CTO): and just to add, latency is ok but we can't expose raw logs offsite, retention windows are super important. regulatory says 7 years for some records, others 90 days, so need to be configurable
[00:50] Jonah (Redwood SE): totally makes sense. on the attestation side we have our SOC2 report and ISO summary, we can share PDFs. for key management we support Redwood-managed KMS, and integrations with customer KMS (BYOK) via envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys
[01:12] Tom (Infra): when you say "customer KMS" is that cross-cloud? we run primary in GCP but some things in Azure, need multi-region key mirroring
[01:26] Jonah: yes we have integrations with GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault; cross-region key sync is something we'd architect with the customer, typically using their KMS replication pattern and Redwood's private deployment options for reduced blast radius
[01:42] Alex: okay, also SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning, must support enforced MFA and RBAC with separation between dev/test and prod
[01:56] Maya: we support SAML/SSO via SAML2 and OIDC; SCIM provisioning with role sync. RBAC can be mapped to SAML groups or to fine-grained roles in the Console. can you tell us who needs admin vs viewer?
[02:12] Priya: admin is only two people, devs get limited run access, ops needs audit access. we also need immutability for audit logs for 1 year and then archive for long term
[02:26] Speaker 4: (mumbling) and log retention... we also have to pass quarterly pen-tests and provide audit log access for our auditors
[02:40] Jonah: we have append-only audit trails, retention policies configurable per-tenant, and export hooks to push logs into your SIEM (splunk, sumo, hum) or secure bucket. auditors can get timeboxed access via signed URLs or read-only accounts
[02:58] Alex: any gotchas around hosted API where data sent to model providers? we have regulatory constraints about data residency and not sending data to external vendor models
[03:12] Maya: good point — for Hosted we only use models vetted and pinned; customers can opt-out of external model routing. Dedicated/Private gives you full control over model binaries and where inference runs, so no third-party routing
[03:28] Tom: cost wise how different is Dedicated vs Private? we might need on-prem for some PHI workloads
[03:40] Jonah: Dedicated is our reserved GPU pools in the cloud — predictable throughput, SLA-backed. Private means customer-managed deployment (VPC or on-prem) with a private control plane and can be air-gapped if needed. Private has higher per-month platform fees but gives max isolation
[03:58] Priya: do you offer hardware-backed attestation, like customers can bring HSMs to on-prem?
[04:08] Jonah: yes, on-prem Private supports HSM/KMS integrations and you can configure the runtime to reference the HSM for key ops. we also support external KMS via gcloud/azure/awskms and to some extent hsm appliances through vault
[04:24] Alex: about RBAC — does Console enforce token-level scoping? we want to ensure service accounts can't read raw inputs post-processing
[04:36] Maya: we have token-level scopes and per-route policies. you can restrict generate vs embeddings vs admin operations. also key rotation is supported with configurable TTLs
[04:50] Speaker 4: quick question: audit logs format? JSON? CSV? we need to run queries for eDiscovery
[05:00] Jonah: logs are JSON structured events with consistent schema, timestamps, correlation IDs. you can ingest them into your SIEM or query via our log export pipeline. retention and archival to encrypted buckets is supported
[05:18] Alex: do you keep KV cache in memory or persisted? i'm worried about PII in cache
[05:26] Jonah: KV cache is in-memory by default and ephemeral per-run but can be persisted for performance in Dedicated; however we offer policies to disable prefix caching for PII-sensitive endpoints, and masking at the prompt layer
[05:42] Priya: masking is good but we need guarantees — do you do redaction at rest?
[05:48] Maya: we support client-side tokenization and redaction patterns; integration with DLP tools is possible. for at-rest storage we use AES-256 and envelope encryption via customer KMS if requested
[06:03] Alex: timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in early July, production Q4. blockers: SOC2 docs, a short perf benchmark on our sample prompts, and validation of KMS integration
[06:18] Maya: ack. we'll send SOC2/ISO and a proposed pilot scope. Jonah will propose sizing and a benchmark plan.

[06:40] (fast forward — technical deep dive segment)
[06:45] Jonah: on technical options — for the Dedicated cluster we recommend pinning model shards to GPUs with quantization profiles; for PHI we usually advise Private with customer KMS and no third-party connectors
[07:02] Tom: around network egress controls — can you restrict outbound to only our VPC endpoints?
[07:10] Jonah: yes Private supports VPC-only egress and restricted network policies. Dedicated can also be configured with private peering and limited egress rules
[07:26] Alex: how do you prove encryption in transit? TLS 1.2/1.3? mutual auth?
[07:34] Maya: TLS 1.3 by default, we support mTLS for Dedicated/Private deployments for service-to-service. SAML assertions are signed; we can provide cert fingerprints and chain
[07:48] Priya: investigations — in the event of an incident what's the SLA for log delivery and forensic support?
[07:56] Jonah: our enterprise support tier includes 24/7 oncall and forensic assistance; we provide stream exports of raw logs and snapshots. we also keep audit trails for all administrative actions with immutable entries
[08:14] Alex: retention policy specifics? ex: metadata 7 years, raw inputs 90 days, embeddings maybe 365?
[08:24] Maya: you can configure retention per data class. defaults are metadata 7 years (archived), raw inputs 90 days, model outputs 180 days, embeddings configurable — we can set 365 for your use case
[08:38] Speaker 4: curious about legal — do you allow contract language for data deletion on termination?
[08:46] Maya: yes contractual data deletion and escrow for keys is standard for Private agreements; for Hosted we have documented data retention and deletion processes, with certificates on request
[09:00] (brief pause)
[09:10] Alex: ok one technical nit — when you do caching, do you do token hashing or reversible storage? we want non-reversible hashes for PII
[09:20] Jonah: we can configure caching to store keyed, salted hashes rather than raw tokens; reversible storage only when you'd like faster retrieval and you provide explicit consent
[09:32] Priya: can we see an example audit log entry?
[09:36] Jonah: i'll attach a sample JSON audit line in the follow-up.

[20:00] (mid-call, around 20 minute mark)
[20:05] Alex: ok on SAML and SCIM provisioning, we want group sync that maps to RBAC roles automatically. can we do fine grain policies like rate limit per team?
[20:16] Maya: yes group sync to roles. rate limiting at tenancy and token level, per-route quotas. also token scoping to limit embedding access etc
[20:28] Tom: what's the process for pen-test? do you provide a testing scope and contact?
[20:34] Jonah: we provide a pen-test engagement doc and have a security mailbox to coordinate; we often require a window and a staging environment if tests are intrusive

[30:40] (later)
[30:45] Maya: to summarize: we'll share SOC2 and ISO attestations, Jonah will outline Dedicated cluster sizing and the pilot benchmark plan, Solace to provide retention matrix and list of systems that need KMS access
[31:02] Alex: agreed. also please include sample contract language for data deletion and key escrow in the packet
[31:10] Maya: noted. we'll also include links to our security whitepaper and the compliance matrix.
[31:18] Jonah: and i'll propose two pilot configs: hosted-with-restrictions (no external model routing) and Dedicated small cluster with BYOK enabled — include cost delta
[31:30] Priya: perfect. one last question — internal auditors want to see certification dates and last pen-test date
[31:38] Maya: we'll include certification dates and last penetration test summary in the packet.

[44:00] (closing)
[44:05] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the attachments and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff. any final Qs?
[44:14] Alex: none, thanks all
[44:16] Priya: thanks
[44:18] Tom: thanks
[44:20] Maya: great, talk soon. bye

References shared during call: security whitepaper (link sent afterwards), SOC2/ISO attestation (to be shared), sample audit log JSON (will attach), pilot benchmark spreadsheet (link to redwood drive)
